minutes.headline: Superintendent warns prior budget cuts are pushing more students toward costly out-of-district special ed placements
minutes.summary: The committee heard a superintendent's report mixing a new DESE-funded reading tutoring grant with a warning that last year's cuts to in-district special education have left the district unable to serve some students, raising the risk of more out-of-district placements. The board discussed FY27 budget level-service figures, decided to stop applying for two small state family-engagement grants and hand them to a regional partner, voted to relocate meetings to the accessible middle-high school, gave the superintendent permission to explore redirecting a legislative earmark from passenger vans to ADA-accessible bathrooms at Turkey Hill, and heard principals describe strained staffing from prior cuts during school improvement plan updates.

budget_items.what_was_said: DESE grant funds one-on-one computer-delivered tutoring for struggling readers at the primary school starting in March, serving all identified below/well-below benchmark students in grades K-2.

budget_items.topic: Student Opportunity Act grant remaining allocation
budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining SOA grant balance covers touch-view screens for the primary school, with most going to fixed costs (instructional support, stipends, summer prep, materials) and the rest to contracted professional development.

First earmarked funds approved this week are going to touch-view screens at the primary school, middle school student needs, and safety improvements (sander attachment and harnesses) across all three campuses.

Funds originally allocated for I-Ready diagnostic assessments and the teacher toolbox will be redirected elsewhere via a coming amendment, since launching the platform this late in the year was judged not worthwhile.
The district currently has 13 out-of-district placements and expects the number could grow because prior budget cuts limited in-district programming capacity.

Superintendent sought permission to ask Rep. Scarsdale to redirect an existing $195,000 transportation earmark toward ADA-accessible bathroom renovations at Turkey Hill instead of buying passenger vans, citing ongoing driver/insurance/maintenance costs the district can't absorb.

Business manager said the level-service budget stands at roughly $28.2 million, with restoration additions discussed at the tri-board meeting adding approximately another amount, including full-family health plan costs for all added positions.
Health insurance with a 14.4% increase is projected to cost about $4.4 million, though the town has not yet finalized that figure.

This year's budget, including an extra $500,000 from the town, was compared to the FY27 level-service and restoration figures to show roughly a $2 million increase for level services and about $2.9 million with restoration positions.
Chapter 70 aid did not increase by much this year, described as a little under a stated figure.

budget_items.topic: CFCE and Parent Child Plus grants
budget_items.what_was_said: Superintendent recommended declining to reapply for these two state family-engagement grants for FY27 due to administrative burden, a retiring coordinator, and declining enrollment, with services expected to transition to a regional partner.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill classroom heater units (Univent coils)
budget_items.what_was_said: Aging classroom heating units at Turkey Hill would cost tens of thousands each to fully replace; maintenance staff instead fabricated replacement coils for a small fraction of that cost per unit.

transfers.description: I-Ready diagnostic assessment/teacher toolbox funds to be reallocated via a coming budget amendment

decisions.decision: Superintendent will not pursue renewal of the CFCE and Parent Child Plus grants for FY27, allowing a regional partner to take over the fiscal agent role; no vote was required.
Board chairs and the town manager will meet separately to set a firm direction before the next tri-board meeting on the override.
Superintendent agreed to resume providing the committee a periodic personnel report.
Superintendent will send the committee and the finance committee an updated staffing/cuts chart reflecting FY26 changes.

what_happened.line: Superintendent said prior budget cuts have limited in-district special education capacity, raising the risk of more costly out-of-district placements.
Superintendent will not seek renewal of two state family-engagement grants for FY27, handing the fiscal-agent role to a regional partner.
Committee voted to move all its meetings to the middle-high school, citing accessibility problems at town hall.
Committee voted, with one abstention, to let the superintendent seek state permission to redirect a passenger-van earmark toward ADA-accessible bathrooms at Turkey Hill.
Business manager presented a level-service FY27 budget figure and a projected double-digit health insurance increase, ahead of the town's own number.

why_it_matters: Out-of-district placements are billed to the town as they occur and are not capped by prior budgets, so a rise here could add pressure to next year's school budget regardless of enrollment.
Moving meetings to the middle-high school changes where residents go to watch or speak on the FY27 budget, including any override vote.
The earmark swap and the two declined grants are one-time or small items next to the level-service total, but they change who administers those programs going forward.
watch_next: Tri-board meeting on the proposed override, after board chairs and the town manager set a direction
Updated staffing/cuts chart the superintendent agreed to send the committee and the finance committee

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the votes that were taken and on most dollar figures tied to the legislative earmarks, SOA grant, and FY27 budget headline numbers. Where they diverge, it is mostly the official minutes omitting entire figures/topics our transcript captured (Chapter 70 change, CFCE/PCP grant dollar amounts, Turkey Hill heater costs, two attendees) and one real ambiguity worth checking: whether meetings moved to "LHS" (per official) or "LMHS" (per ours), and whether "Carla" is a duplicate entry for principal Carla Squier rather than a fourth committee member.
